families.name: From a certificate to a profile
From cell data to the certificate

meaning: Each tie is a pointer that landed. Whether the paper and the Lean say the same thing is a reading.

rows.fidelity_note: The condition requires all fifteen clauses on the same seven groups of cell data. The guide correctly retains that complete hypothesis before drawing the two conclusions.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem has the complete cell condition as its hypothesis and concludes both breakdown statements, exactly as the guide says.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.breakdownOnSpaceAndTorus_of_cell_system_condition

rows.fidelity_note: For every positive viscosity, the formal conclusion gives smooth compactly supported divergence-free initial data with no global smooth solution having one energy bound for all nonnegative times. The smooth recurrent-profile hypothesis is retained.
rows.name: Breakdown.breakdown_on_space

rows.fidelity_note: The formal obstruction quantifies over every global smooth competitor and excludes a single energy bound valid at every nonnegative time; it omits the constructed trajectory and its rate.
rows.name: Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace

rows.fidelity_note: The smooth recurrent profile has velocity derivative bounds through order two and cubic pressure-gradient decay, with a positive period, a rotational recurrence and a nonzero field.
rows.name: Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists

rows.fidelity_note: The transfer statement produces a mild solution starting in any prescribed dense subspace and converging to the recurrent profile after rescaling, with a positive power-law rate.
rows.name: Breakdown.TransferHolds

rows.fidelity_note: This theorem proves the quantitative transfer implication from the spectral dichotomy; that spectral result remains an explicit input, as the passage states.
rows.name: Breakdown.transferHolds_of_dichotomy

rows.fidelity_note: The spectral statement supplies the finite-dimensional exceptional part, forward decay, backward estimates and surjectivity needed by the transfer construction.
rows.name: Breakdown.DichotomyHolds

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem establishes the spectral splitting from the compact-perturbation hypotheses and supplies the remaining input to the transfer argument.
rows.name: Breakdown.dichotomyHolds

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem chooses smooth compactly supported solenoidal initial data and retains a mild trajectory, a recurrent orbit and their positive power-law convergence in similarity variables.
rows.name: Breakdown.exists_blowup_datum

rows.fidelity_note: The construction realizes the evolution by gradient-weighted Fourier fields, with physical embeddings, rotations, dilations and a dense compact-test subspace.
rows.name: Breakdown.Freq.realization

rows.fidelity_note: The physical velocity map is injective and respects rotations and dilations. These are the field identifications required to interpret the rescaled trajectory.
rows.name: Breakdown.FieldReading

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem proves injectivity and the rotation and dilation identities for the concrete Fourier velocity map.
rows.name: Breakdown.fieldReading_realization

rows.fidelity_note: On each fixed closed interval, the mild solution with suitable initial data has a smooth physical velocity and pressure representative with the stated energy and gradient bounds.
rows.name: Breakdown.MildRegular

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem supplies this physical regularity for the Fourier evolution from the heat, bilinear and H¹ identities.
rows.name: Breakdown.mildRegular_realization

rows.fidelity_note: The formal implication retains the smooth recurrent-profile hypothesis and excludes a global smooth solution with periodic velocity for suitable smooth periodic solenoidal data, at every positive viscosity.
rows.name: Breakdown.breakdown_on_torus

rows.fidelity_note: The excluded global competitor is required to have periodic velocity; its pressure is only required to satisfy the smooth solution equations.
rows.name: Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus

rows.fidelity_note: The moving-frame statement keeps the same initial datum and produces periodic velocity and pressure. It imposes no zero-mean requirement on velocity.
rows.name: Breakdown.Periodic.MovingFrameReduction

rows.fidelity_note: The proof chooses a moving frame with zero initial shift and velocity, removing the nonperiodic affine part of pressure while preserving the original datum.
rows.name: Breakdown.Periodic.movingFrameReduction

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.TorusBlowup
ties.plain: A torus mild solution is unbounded

rows.fidelity_note: The internal conclusion is an unbounded mild trajectory on the torus from smooth divergence-free data before a finite terminal time.
rows.name: Breakdown.Periodic.TorusBlowup
rows.plain: A torus mild solution is unbounded

rows.fidelity_note: The formal theorem constructs that trajectory using localization, approximation, comparison, inverse transfer, perturbation and gluing as explicit analytic inputs.
rows.name: Breakdown.Periodic.torusBlowup_of_parts

rows.fidelity_note: The completed argument supplies the torus construction and uniqueness comparison from the given smooth recurrent profile, yielding periodic breakdown.
rows.name: Breakdown.Periodic.breakdownOnTorus_of_profile

rows.fidelity_note: The formal implication starts with the weak recurrent-profile existence condition and concludes whole-space breakdown. The stated integrability, nonzero and recurrence assumptions remain part of that input.
rows.name: Breakdown.breakdown_on_space_of_weak

ties.name: Breakdown.WeakProfile.WeakOrbitOfParts
ties.plain: A weak profile supplies an orbit

rows.fidelity_note: The direct route constructs a continuous recurrent mild orbit from the weak-profile conditions and the listed physical pairing and time-evolution facts.
rows.name: Breakdown.WeakProfile.WeakOrbitOfParts
rows.plain: A weak profile supplies an orbit

rows.fidelity_note: The proof assembles those physical and time-evolution facts to obtain the recurrent mild orbit, retaining them as the hypotheses of the implication.
rows.name: Breakdown.WeakProfile.weakOrbitOfParts_holds

rows.fidelity_note: The completed weak-profile argument constructs the orbit and applies the whole-space transfer argument.
rows.name: Breakdown.breakdownOnSpace_of_weak

rows.fidelity_note: The alternate route obtains a smooth decaying recurrent profile from the weak profile, which is the input used by the periodic argument.
rows.name: Breakdown.FarField.periodicLerayProfileExists_of_weak
rows.plain: Weak profile gives a smooth profile

rows.fidelity_note: The smoothing statement keeps the input period and isometry and identifies the smooth field with the orbit almost everywhere in space at every time.
rows.name: Breakdown.FarField.SmoothFieldOfOrbit

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem establishes that representative for the specified orbit with the same period and isometry.
rows.name: Breakdown.FarField.smoothFieldOfOrbit_holds
rows.plain: Smooth field for a specified orbit

rows.fidelity_note: The final implication returns existence of a smooth recurrent profile without stating its equality to the selected weak field, exactly the loss of correspondence identified here.
rows.name: Breakdown.FarField.periodicLerayProfileExists_of_weak
rows.plain: Weak profile gives a smooth profile

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem concludes existence of a weak recurrent similarity profile from the earlier certificate hypothesis, with that numerical hypothesis retained.
rows.name: Breakdown.certificate_orbit

ties.name: Breakdown.extended_certificate_orbit
ties.plain: A certificate gives a weak profile

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem concludes existence of a weak recurrent similarity profile from the extended certificate hypothesis, with that numerical hypothesis retained.
rows.name: Breakdown.extended_certificate_orbit
rows.plain: A certificate gives a weak profile

rows.fidelity_note: The completed proof supplies the analytic facts needed to pass from the extended certificate to existence of a weak recurrent profile.
rows.name: Breakdown.extended_certificate_orbit_proved

rows.fidelity_note: The assembly takes the analytic estimates and normalization results as explicit inputs and combines them into the extended-certificate implication.
rows.name: Breakdown.Cert.extended_certificate_orbit_of_nodes

rows.fidelity_note: For each admissible parameter, the fixed-point argument supplies the unique correction within the held class; its metric, invariance and bordered-inverse inputs are retained.
rows.name: Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldExistsUniqueHolds_of

rows.fidelity_note: The formal theorem uses held-solution existence, multiplier continuity and the adjoint and stiff-coordinate enclosures to find a parameter with total multiplier zero.
rows.name: Breakdown.Cert.extendedExistsZeroHeldHolds_of

rows.fidelity_note: The finite-dimensional result finds a zero on the specified compact convex parameter set under its continuity and boundary conditions.
rows.name: Breakdown.Held.testSetZero

rows.fidelity_note: The conclusion returns an existential period and weak profile without equations identifying them with the supplied parameter and correction.
rows.name: Breakdown.Cert.ExtendedSigmaProfileOfHeldHolds

rows.fidelity_note: The proof constructs the profile from the chosen parameter and correction, but the theorem’s conclusion only asserts existence and omits those identifying equations.
rows.name: Breakdown.Cert.extendedSigmaProfileOfHeldHolds_of

rows.fidelity_note: The conversion reuses the earlier operator coordinates and sets several unused earlier quantities to zero. It does not assert that the resulting data satisfy the earlier certificate conditions.
rows.name: Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.toCertificateData

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem assumes the full fifteen conditions on the seven shared cell-data groups and concludes the stated whole-space obstruction.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.breakdownOnSpace_of_cell_system_condition

ties.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.breakdownOnTorus_of_cell_system_condition
ties.plain: Obtain conditional blow-up on the torus

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem assumes the same full fifteen conditions on the seven shared cell-data groups and concludes the periodic obstruction.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.breakdownOnTorus_of_cell_system_condition
rows.plain: Obtain conditional blow-up on the torus

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem concludes the conjunction of whole-space and periodic breakdown under the full cell-system hypothesis.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.breakdownOnSpaceAndTorus_of_cell_system_condition

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem supplies the general analytic estimates for cells, traces, rows, tails and the matrix tree, with the numerical cell-entry conditions still required in their applications.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.cellLayerParts_closed

rows.fidelity_note: The condition retains the structural, functional and numerical requirements for the particular shared cell data. The analytic estimates do not themselves supply those data.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The completed whole-space cell argument supplies the analytic implications and retains the full cell-system condition as its input.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.spaceBreakdown_of_cell_system_condition

rows.fidelity_note: The conclusion is an extended certificate after replacing only the decay constant by a suitable real bound. The passage correctly identifies the need to transport any later conclusion that refers to the original decay value.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.isExtendedCertificate_of_parts

rows.fidelity_note: The classical condition has fifteen clauses on the common cell data. It is a different hypothesis from the twelve-clause fractional condition discussed alongside it.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The fractional condition has twelve clauses and fixes the exponent to 501/500. It is distinct from the classical fifteen-clause cell condition.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: This row specifies the quantitative transfer statement. The later conditional arguments and their supplied analytic proofs are separate rows.
rows.name: Breakdown.TransferHolds

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem derives transfer from the step-data solver, contraction, perturbation, profile-piece and gluing facts, retaining those five analytic inputs.
rows.name: Breakdown.transferHolds_of

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem supplies the intermediate transfer ingredients and retains the spectral dichotomy as its remaining analytic input.
rows.name: Breakdown.transferHolds_of_dichotomy

rows.fidelity_note: Every element of the closed Fourier graph has the required relation between its gradient and second-derivative components.
rows.name: Breakdown.Cert.GraphClosedHolds

rows.fidelity_note: For each element of the graph, this theorem establishes that relation directly from membership in the closed graph.
rows.name: Breakdown.Cert.halfSsp_of_xbar

rows.fidelity_note: The physical representative has the same weighted energy, gradient norm and pin pairings as the Fourier graph element.
rows.name: Breakdown.Cert.ReadingEnergyHolds

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem obtains those physical energy and pin identities using the derivative relation for every graph element as its hypothesis.
rows.name: Breakdown.Cert.readingEnergyHolds_of

rows.fidelity_note: For a smooth decaying field, the squared Fourier-space norm equals the sum of the three physical squared derivative L² norms.
rows.name: Breakdown.Freq.EmbedNorm

rows.fidelity_note: The embedding preserves addition, subtraction and real scalar multiplication on smooth decaying fields, which is the linearity component named in the passage.
rows.name: Breakdown.Freq.EmbedLinear

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem proves both the norm identity and linearity. A link to one component should retain which of those two conclusions is intended.
rows.name: Breakdown.Freq.embedNormLinear_holds

rows.fidelity_note: For 1<α<5/4, a rotating fractional similarity profile implies the corresponding whole-space fractional breakdown statement.
rows.name: Breakdown.fractional_breakdown_on_space

rows.fidelity_note: For 1<α<5/4, a rotating fractional similarity profile implies the corresponding periodic fractional breakdown statement.
rows.name: Breakdown.fractional_breakdown_on_torus

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem obtains a rotating fractional profile from the fractional certificate for 1<α<5/4. This is the separate fractional implication named by the passage.
rows.name: Breakdown.SteadyCert.fracCertificate_profile

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem concludes both fractional breakdown statements at α=501/500 from its separate twelve-clause fractional cell condition.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellCert.CellSystem.fractional_breakdown_of_cell_system

topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.
topics.name: The fractional extension

topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).
topics.name: The blow-up statements

topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).
topics.name: Passing to the torus

topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).
topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions

topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).
topics.name: Monodromy and the correction

topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).
topics.name: Recurrent profiles

topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).
topics.name: From certificate to profile

topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).
topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate

topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.
topics.name: Encoded cell data

topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).
topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane

topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).
topics.name: Cells, traces and tails

topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).
topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests

topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).
topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound

topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).
topics.name: Changing the profile

topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).
topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error

topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).
topics.name: The offset and the certificate
